en.commentary: I have hauled portable monitors through airports, coffee shops, and a few too many hotel desks, and 2026 is the year the category finally stopped asking you to compromise. The ASUS ZenScreen OLED MQ16AH takes the top spot because it nails the one thing a second screen has to do: disappear into your bag and then look stunning the moment you plug it in. At 360 grams it weighs less than most tablets, and the OLED panel hits 100% DCI-P3 with a measured Delta E under 2, so the colors are accurate enough that I trust it for photo culling on the road. The espresso Display 15 Touch lands at number two on the strength of real touchscreen utility. Marking up a PDF with my finger or dragging layers in a design app changes how I work away from the desk, and the aluminium and glass build feels worth the $349. Value tells the rest of the story this year. The ViewSonic TD1656-2K delivers a 16-inch 2.5K touch panel with a 65W cable and a real stand for under $300, which is the best balance of resolution, size, and price on the list. At the bottom of the budget range, the Arzopa Z1FC gives console and laptop gamers a 144Hz screen for $119, and it genuinely embarrasses panels that cost twice as much. USB-C with single-cable power is now the baseline, OLED is the upgrade worth paying for, and touch is the feature that earns its keep for anyone who works on the move.

This is the screen I hand to anyone who wants a second display without overthinking the purchase.

en.commentary:
No portable monitor shipped this week, so the board holds, but two items are worth putting on your radar.

ASUS showed the ZenScreen OLED 14 at Computex this year: 8 millimetres thick, under 500 grams, a 1920 by 1200 OLED panel at 90 percent DCI-P3, and dual USB-C with 85 watt passthrough. That passthrough number is the detail I care about. It means one cable to your laptop carries video and charges the laptop at the same time, which is the difference between a monitor you actually pack and one that stays in a drawer. When it lands it will pressure the top of this list.

UPERFECT is taking deposits on the Omega, a foldable OLED portable monitor concept aimed at roughly 2,500 dollars. That is a deposit on a concept, so treat it as a curiosity rather than a purchase.

Today the ASUS ZenScreen OLED MQ16AH stays at rank 1 with 9.2 overall. A 9.6 on image quality and 9.4 on portability is the balance this category is actually about, and the OLED black level makes a real difference when you are working in a dim hotel room.

The espresso Display 15 Touch at rank 2 earns its place on a 9.5 versatility score. Touch input plus the magnetic stand system means it works as a second screen, a drawing surface, and a propped up reference panel without buying accessories.

On value, the Arzopa Z1FC at rank 6 posts 9.8. A 16.1 inch 144Hz panel at that price is the easiest recommendation for anyone who just needs more pixels on the road.

預算取向的話，第 6 名的 Arzopa Z1FC 值得標 9.8。16.1 吋 144Hz 賣這個價，只是想在外面多一塊螢幕的人，看這台就可以收工了。
